division_reconstructed.note: No source places this household anywhere — the record gives a name and no address, no street and not even a division. So BOTH halves of this band are dealt rather than read: the south division from the reconstruction order book's own household target by division, and the class from the town model's employment distribution, which puts this household under the placement policy's merchant_and_professional_dwellings clause. The better houses take the Randolph–Washington tier a block back from the trade, and the north tier under Kinzie: off the noise, on dry ground, with a garden. Inferred — the town holds one documented H roof and it is Cobweb Castle, on the north side, which is itself the clause's own outlier. The deal is seeded on this household's own id, so it is the same on every run — and it is the weakest seat this ladder makes: no lot, no roof, no coordinate and no source behind either half of it.

married.what_happened: NOT DRAWN FOR THIS HOUSE: MOVED INTO IT. The household model drew this house married and the order book had no woman left in its wife's cell, so no wife was drawn. Phebe Bardwell headed a house of her own, dealt by T-1174 to fill the women and children the age pyramid lacked; she fits this house by its own rules — her division, a band never above his, no child older than his band allows — and T-2020 folds her house into his: she is his wife here and the 6 of her house come with her. Every name, age band and seed is the one T-1174 drew; the children keep the surname they were dealt with. Both people are the town's invention at the `reconstructed` tier, and the marriage is too: no source says L Franchere married anybody.

associated_with.note: THE REGISTER NAMES HIM AT A PARISH ACT, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE OF THE CLAIM. Father St. Cyr's register carries this person as witness in st_cyr_marriage_001_3, dated 1834 and tied to this card by the church crosswalk's rule G2c. `st_marys_church` is his church, which the structure record states — 'St. Cyr selected the lot in 1833 and ... was succeeded by Father O'Meara only after 1837, so he is the pastor across the whole scene window'. THIS IS NOT A MEMBERSHIP ROW: being a witness, a party or a decedent at a Catholic act is what the register states, and the dates are the act's own, which is why `from` and `to` are the same day and the row is not carried forward to the scene date.

merge_ruling.for_merge: One man is the likely reading and both cards stand on FATHER ST CYR'S OWN HAND. 'L. Franchere' is a witness in the St Cyr register (ICHR v4) in 1834; 'Louis Franchère' is a sponsor in St Mary's baptismal register on 5 June 1833. L agrees with Louis as an initial stands for a forename, the surname is one name — Franchère — and the apparent one-letter gap is this project's own transcription, one source printing the grave accent and the other not. Neither stem is otherwise populated: one card each, and Franchere is set three times in three texts while Franchre is set nowhere at all, because it is not a spelling anybody used. READ AGAIN BY T-1554, AND NOTHING ON THE PAGE CUTS AGAINST IT: the Review's tabulation of the marriage (vol. 4, July 1921) sets the witness at the first marriage St Cyr entered at Chicago, beside T. B. Beubien, with nothing about him that the sponsor of 5 June 1833 contradicts; and the 1833 petition of Chicago's Catholics to Bishop Rosati, which the Review printed in vol. 3 (January 1921, p. 231), lists 'Francherez, Louis 1' among the heads of family, so a Louis of the stem was a Catholic at Chicago in the year of the baptism. That is a Louis again, not an L., and the petition is not yet a source this project holds.
merge_ruling.against_merge: THE PAGE WAS READ AND IT PRINTS THE INITIAL. T-1554 read every printing of this entry this project can reach, on 2026-10-09, and each sets 'L. Franchere': the Genealogy Trails page (data/research/church/text/st_cyr_marriages_1834_1839.txt, line 7) and, behind it, the Illinois Catholic Historical Review vol. 4, July 1921, 'The First Chicago Marriage Records', first row ('-1834 | N. Murphy, Mrs. M. Frauner | L. Franchere, T. B. Beubien | J. M. I. Saint Cyr'), in two independent archive.org scans of the volume (illinoiscatholic04illi_0 and illinoiscatholic04unse). So the web transcription is faithful and the 1921 tabulator gave no forename either; T-1525's premise that 'reading that entry for a full forename settles it' is spent on every printing. NOR IS ANY ONE TITLE CAUGHT SETTING BOTH: the Review tabulated the baptisms in vol. 3 no. 4 (April 1921, pp. 406-408, archive.org illinoiscatholic03unse_2) and its table runs from the entry of 26 May 1833 straight to 15 May 1834, omitting the entry of 5 June 1833 where the deposited scan reads 'Louis Franchère'. So the Review sets 'Franchere' without its accent in the one place and nowhere sets the other, and the cards' 'franchre' is this project's extraction dropping the è (T-2197 recorded that for this card). C2 would fold an initial onto its one full forename, but it does so on a surname the two printings share, and C9 and C10 ask for the printer's own demonstration that two settings are one name; neither is in hand, and the accent is not to be waved through on the merge it would decide. THE ANSWER IS STILL ON A PAGE, AND THE PAGE EXISTS: the Review (vol. 3, p. 405) quotes the register's fly leaf — 'This record of baptisms and marriages solemnized from the year 1833-39 … was collected and bound by me in the year 1880. Jos. P. Rouges, Rector' — so the marriage is entered in the same book whose title page and pages 1-19 are deposited at chicago/reference/catholic-baptisms-1833-1835/, in St Cyr's own hand. Its marriage leaves are not deposited. U1 stands and T-2251 owns depositing and reading that leaf.

age_band.note: AN AGE BAND, NEVER A YEAR. No source this project holds bears on when this person was born, so the band is drawn from the only committed sex by age distribution the project has - the 1840 Chicago schedule, five years after the scene and a town twice the size - seeded by this person's own id ('franchere_l:age_bands_1840'). AND THE CONDITIONING IS THE MODEL'S, NOT A SOURCE'S: that a roll naming a person in their own right names somebody 15 or over. The 1840 schedule counts a child as a tally inside a household and never as a correspondent; 15 rather than 20 because an apprentice or a journeyman stands on a trade roll. No source states this rule. No exact year is written, because a year drawn from a decadal band would read as a record of a birth.

superseded_record.research_note: MINTED FROM THE CONSOLIDATED CIVIC, CHURCH, PRESS, BOOK AND CENSUS EVIDENCE (T-0513, T-0514). THE HOUSEHOLD IS A CONTAINER, NOT AN ARGUMENT: every other record here is written unattested in its own block, because the lists that name this person name a person and not a family. What is claimed is that the sources cited on the member below name them at Chicago, and the grade is the owner's ratified ladder applied by tools/consolidate_resident_evidence.py --build and spent by tools/mint_civic_residents.py, which prints every refusal. docs/LIBERTIES.md L215 carries the liberty and the tension with L213.
